test.fullName: UpdateItem — validation ordering rejects invalid ReturnValues (UpdateItem reports the first enum error)

splits.behaviour: UpdateItem with invalid ReturnValues and ReturnConsumedCapacity: part of the 2026-06 validation-framework rollout. New-cohort regions stop at the first invalid enum and report one error; old-cohort regions aggregate both. ap-northeast-1, ap-south-2, ap-southeast-6, ap-southeast-7, ca-central-1, eu-central-2, eu-south-1, eu-west-1 and us-east-2 crossed to the new cohort by the 2026-10-03 sweep, which three runs from separate processes on 2026-10-07 confirmed. eu-south-2 followed by the 2026-10-24 sweep, which agreed with three runs from separate processes on 2026-10-22, leaving me-central-1 the only old-cohort region. On 2026-11-14 the single-error cohort split in two: the 19 regions that began accepting a 32-level ExpressionAttributeValue that day (row update-item-nesting-depth-expression-value), eu-west-2 among them, began listing UPDATED_NEW in the enum set where they had listed UPDATE_NEW. Three runs from separate processes that day agreed, so the pinned answer is now the UPDATED_NEW wording. ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-6, ap-southeast-7 and ap-south-2 changed during those runs and are recorded by their last, which listed UPDATED_NEW. The ten regions still listing UPDATE_NEW are recorded on it, me-central-1 among them: it gave the single-error form on the 2026-11-14 sweep and on all three runs, where it had reported both errors on every sweep before. The test asserts the single-error envelope and the enum phrase, so it passes both wordings, and this row is where the exact answers are pinned. The 2026-11-21 sweep found ap-east-1, ap-southeast-2, ca-west-1, eu-south-2, eu-west-3, mx-central-1, us-east-1, us-west-1 and us-west-2 giving the pinned answer, so they are recorded on it. Every region that answered now agrees with eu-west-2 except me-central-1, which gave its recorded answer on that sweep and stays recorded on it; it has been out of the observed set since the 2026-10-31 sweep.

test.fullName: Nesting depth — 32-level document limit accepts a 32-level ExpressionAttributeValue (condition is evaluated)

splits.behaviour: UpdateItem carrying a 32-level ExpressionAttributeValue. 32 is the documented limit, so this is a boundary disagreement rather than a violation: some regions refuse the value in validation, the rest accept it and go on to evaluate the condition. The condition compares an attribute the item never has, so it is false everywhere and a ConditionalCheckFailedException is proof the value was accepted rather than a sign of differing regional state. Until the 2026-11-07 sweep the pinned eu-west-2 refused it, and from the 2026-10-24 sweep every answering region but me-central-1 did. The 2026-11-14 sweep found 19 regions, eu-west-2 among them, accepting it: af-south-1, ap-east-2, ap-northeast-2, ap-northeast-3, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-3, ap-southeast-4, ap-southeast-5, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-central-2, eu-north-1, eu-south-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, il-central-1, sa-east-1 and us-east-2. Three runs from separate processes later that day agreed, so the pinned answer is now acceptance and the test asserts the ConditionalCheckFailedException. ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-6, ap-southeast-7 and ap-south-2 changed answer during those three runs and are recorded by their last, which accepted. ap-east-1, ap-southeast-2, ca-west-1, eu-south-2, eu-west-3, mx-central-1, us-east-1, us-west-1 and us-west-2 refused it on the sweep and on every run, and me-central-1, which had accepted it on every sweep before, refused it on the 2026-11-14 sweep and on all three runs. Those ten are recorded on the refusing side, and this row is the only place their exact message is pinned. The same regions moved on the ReturnValues enum message the same day (row update-item-validation-error-aggregation). The 2026-11-21 sweep found ap-east-1, ap-southeast-2, ca-west-1, eu-south-2, eu-west-3, mx-central-1, us-east-1, us-west-1 and us-west-2 giving the pinned answer, so they are recorded on it. Every region that answered now agrees with eu-west-2 except me-central-1, which gave its recorded answer on that sweep and stays recorded on it; it has been out of the observed set since the 2026-10-31 sweep.
